S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder is defined by at least one manic episode, marked by a distinct period of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased energy and clinically significant impairment. Episodes often emerge in a recurrent course and may be recognized when confidence, activity, sleep reduction, and distractibility disrupt work, relationships, or safety. Its key distinction from Bipolar II Disorder is the presence of full mania rather than hypomania alone.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient.stressor: Martha was asked to take over a large multi-site spectroscopy project after a senior investigator stepped back, placing grant deadlines, graduate-student supervision, and instrument scheduling under her authority. What began as disciplined overcommitment turned over seven months into a markedly elevated and irritable drive to redesign the lab’s direction, with very little sleep, grand confidence that she alone could solve every technical barrier, and attention repeatedly pulled toward side problems unrelated to the core experiments. The change became clinically significant when her impaired judgment and distractibility disrupted lab operations, strained mentoring relationships, and jeopardized a major grant milestone despite her previously meticulous reputation. She came to psychiatric care through an emergency assessment arranged by her spouse and department leadership after a lab-safety meeting made clear that her functioning had substantially deteriorated.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: I came in because I can't keep my mind on the actual experiment anymore—during a grant call or safety meeting I'll notice a pump vibration, a student's side comment, or some odd peak in an old spectrum and suddenly I'm off chasing that for hours while the thing everyone needs from me falls apart.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: For months I've felt like the lab is finally moving at my speed, almost electrified, but if someone questions my plan or asks me to slow down I snap at them in a way that has made students avoid my office.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I'm at the lab before anyone arrives, rewriting protocols, rearranging instrument schedules, emailing collaborators in three countries, and starting new analyses all at once because sitting still feels like wasting the one chance to fix everything.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: I genuinely believed I could rescue the entire multi-site project by myself, redesign the spectroscopy approach, mentor every student better than their advisors, and still beat the grant deadline if people would just stop getting in my way.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: Most nights I sleep two or three hours, sometimes on the couch with my laptop open, and I wake up sharp and ready to work instead of tired, like sleep is an inefficient interruption.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: My department has had to step in on decisions I used to handle because missed priorities, confused scheduling, and strained supervision started putting the project and lab safety expectations at risk.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about seven months, since I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project.
